input.question: Which award did Samuel Yellen receive?

documents.text:
**Renowned American Novelist Samuel Yellen Honored with Prestigious Guggenheim Fellowship**

In a testament to his outstanding contributions to American literature, acclaimed novelist Samuel Yellen has been awarded the esteemed Guggenheim Fellowship, a prestigious grant recognizing excellence in the arts. Established in 1925, the Guggenheim Fellowship is one of the most coveted honors in the literary world, with past recipients including literary giants such as Ernest Hemingway, Langston Hughes, and Toni Morrison. This year, the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation has selected Samuel Yellen as one of its distinguished fellows, acknowledging his remarkable body of work and commitment to the craft of novel writing. "We are thrilled to recognize Samuel Yellen's remarkable talent and dedication to his craft," said Dr. Edward Hirsch, President of the John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation. "His novels have captivated readers with their nuanced exploration of the human experience, and we are confident that this fellowship will enable him to continue pushing the boundaries of literary excellence." Yellen's writing has been praised for its lyrical prose, complex characters, and thought-provoking themes. His novels have been widely acclaimed by critics and readers alike, with many noting his unique ability to capture the essence of the American experience. "Samuel Yellen is a masterful storyteller, and this fellowship is a well-deserved recognition of his remarkable talent," said Pulitzer Prize-winning author, Michael Cunningham. "His writing has a way of getting under your skin, staying with you long after you finish reading his books. He is a true artist, and I have no doubt that this fellowship will enable him to continue producing work that will leave a lasting impact on American literature." According to the Guggenheim Foundation, Yellen's fellowship will provide him with the financial support and creative freedom to pursue his next literary project. The foundation awards approximately 175 fellowships annually, with recipients selected from a pool of over 3,000 applicants. Data from the Guggenheim Foundation reveals that since its inception, the fellowship has supported some of the most influential writers of the 20th and 21st centuries, with over 80% of fellows going on to publish critically acclaimed works. In a statement, Yellen expressed his gratitude for the recognition, saying, "I am deeply humbled to be included among such an esteemed group of writers.
